title: Multi-query and step-back
summary: Multi-query fans one question out into several variants, retrieves for each and fuses the results. Step-back adds a more general question so the retriever also finds background and principles.
useIf: Recall is low because a single phrasing misses relevant chunks, or the answer depends on a general principle the specific question does not name.
avoidIf: Precision is the problem, the question is multi-part (use decomposition), or each extra search is too costly.

explain.md: **Multi-query.** A model writes N alternative phrasings or angles of the question. Each runs as its own search, and the ranked lists are merged, commonly with reciprocal rank fusion. RAG-Fusion packages this idea as multiple generated queries plus RRF. Its author found answers were more accurate and comprehensive, but some drifted off topic when generated queries were not relevant enough to the original [[tr4]]. Azure's preview `queryRewrites: "generative|count-N"` does the fan-out inside the service, with N from 1 to 10 [[r28]].

**Step-back.** Step-back prompting asks the model to derive a higher-level concept or principle before reasoning. The paper reports gains on reasoning tasks: PaLM-2L improved about 7% on MMLU Physics and 11% on Chemistry, 27% on TimeQA and 7% on MuSiQue [[r15]]. Those numbers are for reasoning benchmarks, not retrieval. In RAG the practical use is to retrieve for both the specific question and its abstraction, so the model receives the details and the governing rule.

explain.title: Fan-out, fuse and dedupe
explain.alt: A question is expanded into variants and a step-back question, each searched in parallel, then merged with fusion and duplicates removed before reranking.
explain.src:
flowchart LR
  Q[Question] --> M[LLM expansion]
  M --> V1[Variant 1]
  M --> V2[Variant 2]
  M --> SB[Step-back question]
  Q --> O[Original query]
  V1 --> F[Fuse and dedupe]
  V2 --> F
  SB --> F
  O --> F
  F --> R[Rerank]

explain.md: **Costs and controls.** N variants mean N searches (in Azure each extra query counts as another execution [[r1]]), one generation call before them, and many duplicate chunks. Dedupe by chunk id before reranking, keep the original query as one of the lists, cap N (3 to 5 is a common starting point, author suggestion) and let a reranker restore precision after the fusion.

explain.title: Variants widen recall and also noise
explain.md: Every off-topic variant pulls off-topic chunks into the fusion. Measure precision at the cutoff, not only recall, and drop variants whose lists share nothing with the original.

whereToUse: Short or ambiguous questions where one phrasing misses documents
Corpora with varied vocabulary, such as support articles from several authors
Science and engineering questions where a general principle explains the answer
Pipelines already using RRF, where extra lists fit naturally

use: Recall at the shortlist is the weak point
Questions are ambiguous or vocabulary varies
You can afford N parallel searches
avoid: The failure is a multi-part question, where sub-questions beat paraphrases
Latency or search cost is strictly capped
Identifiers dominate and variants drift away from them
flips: Questions have independent sub-parts: switch to decomposition
Variants add noise: reduce N or require overlap with the original list
A background rule matters: add a step-back question beside the specific one

pitfalls.symptom: Answers wander into related but unasked topics
pitfalls.cause: Generated variants strayed from the original intent and fused noisy chunks [[tr4]]
pitfalls.fix: Keep the original list, cap N, and require agreement or rerank before the cutoff

pitfalls.symptom: The same chunk appears many times in the context
pitfalls.cause: Variants retrieved overlapping results and no dedupe ran
pitfalls.fix: Deduplicate by chunk id after fusion and before reranking

pitfalls.symptom: Costs and latency grew with no recall gain
pitfalls.cause: Variants were near-paraphrases of the same words
pitfalls.fix: Ask for diverse angles and measure list overlap. Reduce N when overlap is high

scenarios.title: Ambiguous short questions, recall is low
scenarios.situation: Users type three-word questions such as 'reset access token'. The corpus uses several terms for the same thing. Offline tests show the gold chunk appears at rank 12 on average.
constraints: A few extra searches are affordable
scenarios.question: What do you try?

options.name: Multi-query with N of 3 plus the original, fuse with RRF, dedupe and rerank
options.why: Variants cover vocabulary variation, the original anchors intent and the reranker restores precision.
options.tradeoff: Three extra searches and one generation per query.

options.name: Increase chunk overlap
options.why: It targets ingestion boundaries, not vocabulary mismatch.
options.tradeoff: Useful when answers straddle chunk boundaries.

options.name: Replace the query with one rewrite
options.tradeoff: One guess at the right wording and a drift risk.

flips.if: Precision at the cutoff drops after fan-out
flips.then: Reduce N and require overlap with the original list.

flips.if: No reranker exists and each extra search costs real money
flips.then: Use a single rewrite or the original query alone, since fan-out without a reranker mostly adds noise.

scenarios.takeaway: Fan out for recall, rerank for precision.

scenarios.title: Physics tutor with specific problems
scenarios.situation: Students ask specific problems, for example about the pressure of a gas after heating. The answer needs the general law, and the textbook states laws in separate sections.
unknowns: Does the corpus label sections by principle?
Can the model name the principle reliably?
scenarios.question: Which transformation fits?

options.name: Step-back: retrieve for the specific question and for the principle behind it, merge, then answer
options.why: Step-back showed its gains on physics and chemistry reasoning [[r15]], and the textbook stores principles separately from examples.
options.tradeoff: An extra generation and retrieval. The paper's numbers are for reasoning, not for retrieval metrics.

options.name: Multi-query paraphrases
options.why: Improves recall for the specific wording.
options.tradeoff: Does not add the general law.

options.name: HyDE with a hypothetical solution
options.why: A wrong worked solution can pull in wrong examples.
options.tradeoff: Fits short factual queries where an answer-shaped passage helps.

flips.if: The question is a simple definition
flips.then: Skip step-back and use a plain query.

flips.if: Questions are short and ambiguous rather than specific
flips.then: Prefer multi-query paraphrases, since there is no specific detail to abstract away from.

scenarios.takeaway: Step-back retrieves the rule behind the example.

quiz.q: After adding multi-query, the context contains the same chunk four times and token cost rose. What step is missing?
options: Deduplication by chunk id after fusion
quiz.explain: Variants retrieve overlapping chunks. Dedupe after fusion before reranking. The other options do not remove duplicates.

quiz.q: Which question shape is better served by decomposition than by multi-query?
options: A question that compares two regions across two time periods
quiz.explain: Compound comparisons have distinct sub-questions that must each be answered. Paraphrases do not cover them. The other shapes suit rewriting or multi-query.

quiz.q: Select the statements consistent with the sources.
options: RAG-Fusion generates multiple queries and fuses with RRF
Step-back reported gains on reasoning tasks, not retrieval metrics
quiz.explain: RAG-Fusion, the step-back paper and the Azure page support the first three. The RAG-Fusion study itself noted off-topic drift when generated queries strayed [[tr4]].

flashcards.back: Generate multiple queries, retrieve for each and merge the lists with reciprocal rank fusion.
Ask for a higher-level concept or principle first, then reason. In RAG, retrieve for both the specific and the abstract question.

flashcards.front: Name two controls that keep multi-query cheap and clean.
flashcards.back: Cap N and dedupe by chunk id. Keep the original query as one list and rerank after fusion.
